query: 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis latest status July 2026 - are attacks on ships continuing or has there been a ceasefire/truce? UKMTO attack incidents in Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz, Gulf of Oman in July 2026
answer:
Research complete. Summary of what I found:

**The direct answer to the question: attacks are continuing, and there is no ceasefire.**

The 17 June Islamabad MoU — the truce that was supposed to reopen the strait — collapsed on 7–8 July when Trump declared it "over," and its 60-day window **formally expired on 17 August 2026** with no extension. Trump announced the following day that there are "no talks or conversations going on, or scheduled" with Iran.

**July 2026 was one of the worst months of the crisis.** I reconstructed the UKMTO incident log from the JMIC advisory notes and individual warning PDFs: roughly 20 incidents, including three tankers struck on 7 July (which triggered JMIC raising the strait to SEVERE, where it has stayed ever since), four attacks on 13 July alone (two with fatalities/serious injuries), and two vessels abandoned by their crews on 20–21 July. There was a genuine lull from ~23–30 July — JMIC confirmed no new attacks on 28 July — but traffic simultaneously hit crisis lows (one tanker crossed on 23 July).

**Attacks have since accelerated.** JMIC's latest advisory (Update 086, 18 Aug) states outright that "attack frequency against commercial shipping in the Strait has increased," linking it to the MoU lapse. The most recent confirmed attack was 18 August: the bulker *Minoan Dignity*, chief engineer killed.

Two things worth flagging that go slightly beyond the question as posed:

- **The southern Omani corridor is the kill zone** — 14 of 16 projectile strikes since 6 July. This is not random violence; Iran is systematically punishing use of the US/Oman route to force traffic onto its own unilateral northern route, and it is working (90/10 route split by late July).
- **Iran added a detention vector on 17 August**, claiming to have seized a UAE-owned tanker for not paying transit service fees. That is a different risk category from kinetic attack and is new.

One caveat on completeness: UKMTO warning numbers 096–100 and 106, 109, 113 don't appear in any public index I could reach, so the July log may omit 2–4 incidents between 23 and 31 July. The JMIC running count (68 on 19 Jul → 91 on 18 Aug) is the more reliable aggregate. I also found the Wikipedia "List of ships attacked" article badly incomplete — no August entries at all — so I worked from the UKMTO/JMIC primary documents instead.

sources.title: Update 086 to JMIC Advisory Note: 01 March - 18 August 2026
sources.snippet: Regional Threat Level: SEVERE. Total of 91 incidents since 01 March; two incidents since the last report. 18 August 2026, UKMTO 115-26: general cargo ship transiting southbound through the Strait of Hormuz, 0.5NM from the coast of Oman - vessel was struck by an unknown projectile in its engine room; one crew fatality reported. 'Attack frequency against commercial shipping in the Strait has increased over the reporting period... may coincide with Iranian claims of a shift in posture now that the 60-day period following the 17 June U.S.-Iran MOU has lapsed.' U.S.-facilitated SoH transits 16-17 August (past 48 hours): 42, against a historical average of ~138 vessels/day.

sources.title: 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
sources.snippet: Crisis began 28 February 2026 with Operation Epic Fury. Key ceasefires: 8 April Iran-US temporary ceasefire; 17 June Islamabad Memorandum; 19 June Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire (collapsed within a day, strait reclosed 20 June); interim truce broke down 8 July after renewed ship attacks. No durable ceasefire has held; hostilities and shipping attacks continued through mid-August 2026. Infobox lists no end date.

sources.title: US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding expires: How and why it fell apart
sources.snippet: The June 17 MoU between the United States and Iran expired on Monday amid faltering talks. The 14-point MoU was signed on June 17 between Pezeshkian and Trump, triggering a 60-day negotiating period. Iran pledged to clear mines from the Strait of Hormuz and allow ships to pass 'with no charge' for 60 days; the US agreed to end its naval blockade within 30 days. The MoU collapsed within a month. On July 7, Trump declared that the agreement was 'over'. Negotiations have reached a deadlock.

sources.title: Trump says no talks planned with Iran amid anger over Iran-Oman Hormuz deal
sources.snippet: 'There are no talks or conversations going on, or scheduled, with the Islamic Republic of Iran. The Naval Blockade remains in full force and effect. The Hormuz Strait is open and operating. All water mines have been removed or detonated,' Trump posted. He also posted a map of the Strait captioned 'New US Territory'. Iranian negotiator Ghalibaf said the Strait would remain shut until the US met MoU conditions.

sources.title: Vessel hit by 'unknown projectile' in Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO says
sources.snippet: A vessel struck by an 'unknown projectile' while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, causing damage to the engine room and resulting in a crew casualty. Shipping through the Strait remains severely disrupted, with daily vessel crossings in the single digits, down from more than 130 a day before the war.

sources.title: Iran, US set new conditions during Hormuz talks: What does this mean?
sources.snippet: Six new conditions announced by Iran's Supreme National Security Council: an end to US threats and insults; a permanent end to attacks against Iran and its allies in Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen and Iraq; the lifting of the US naval blockade and withdrawal of US forces; compensation for damage from two 'imposed wars'; the lifting of sanctions; the unconditional release of frozen Iranian assets.

sources.title: Iran says it will escalate if US does not honour deal within weeks
sources.snippet: Iran will escalate tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and beyond, and launch an attack if the U.S. fails to implement an interim peace deal fully in a matter of weeks, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Monday. Tehran would conduct a 'timely and precise' military attack to break the U.S. naval blockade.

sources.title: Iran war is far from over as deadline for a deal passes
sources.snippet: The deal Trump signed at Versailles in June set an ambitious 60-day deadline. The deadline was Monday, and the two sides are further apart than they were then. Talks have focused on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and lifting a U.S. blockade, both of which were supposed to have happened under the interim deal. There has been no sign of any compromise on the strait.

sources.title: Ship attacked in Hormuz strait as Iran throttles traffic through key waterway
sources.snippet: Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz dropped significantly last week, with confirmed crossings falling 19.5% to 95 transits. Only three vessels made it through the waterway on Sunday, according to Kpler. An unidentified projectile damaged the engine room of a ship near Oman and 'resulted in a crew casualty'.

key_facts: NO CEASEFIRE IS IN FORCE as of 19 August 2026. The 17 June 2026 US-Iran Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding collapsed in early July (Trump declared it 'over' on 7 July) and its 60-day negotiating window formally EXPIRED on Monday 17 August 2026 with no extension and no successor deal.

ATTACKS ARE CONTINUING AND ACCELERATING. JMIC Update 086 (18 Aug 2026) states verbatim: 'Attack frequency against commercial shipping in the Strait has increased over the reporting period... may coincide with Iranian claims of a shift in posture now that the 60-day period following the 17 June U.S.-Iran MOU has lapsed.'

JMIC has held the Strait of Hormuz at threat level SEVERE ('deliberate hostile action highly likely') continuously since 7 July 2026, when three merchant ships were struck in one day. It had briefly been downgraded to MODERATE on 18 June under JMIC Advisory 009-26 'Strait of Hormuz Open'.

Most recent confirmed attack: 18 August 2026 (UKMTO 115-26) - Liberia-flagged bulker Minoan Dignity struck by unknown projectile in the engine room 0.5NM off the Omani coast while outbound; Filipino chief engineer killed; two helicopter evacuation attempts failed. Second Modion Maritime bulker hit in a fortnight.

JMIC confirmed incident count since 1 March 2026: 68 (19 Jul) -> 72 (21 Jul) -> 83 (6 Aug) -> 84 (9 Aug) -> 91 (18 Aug). JMIC Update 074 noted 'Iranian attacks, fourteen since 25 June' kept the level at SEVERE.

July 2026 UKMTO Hormuz/Gulf of Oman attack incidents: 080/081/082-26 (7 Jul, three tankers incl. Qatari LNG Al Rekayat and Saudi VLCC Wedyan); 083-26 (11 Jul, container ship GFS Galaxy, 1 Indian crew dead); 085-26, 086-26 (Mombasa B, multiple serious injuries), 087-26 (Al Bahyah, 1 fatality) on 13 Jul; Stolt Magnesium 14 Jul; 089-26 (15 Jul); 088-26 (17 Jul); 092-26 (20 Jul, Kavomaleas, crew abandoned ship); 093-26 (20 Jul, off Dibba UAE); 094-26 (21 Jul, crew abandoned into lifeboat); 101-26 and 102-26 (31 Jul, LNG carrier Gaslog Shanghai lost propulsion).

There was a LULL in Strait of Hormuz attacks from roughly 23-30 July 2026 - JMIC confirmed on 28 July no new attacks in the prior 48 hours - but traffic simultaneously fell to crisis lows (only 1 tanker crossed on 23 July, the lowest since 7 May).

UKMTO reported the southern Omani corridor accounted for 14 of the 16 projectile-strike incidents since 6 July 2026. Iran does not recognise the US/Oman-backed southern route and attacks vessels using it to force traffic onto its own unilateral northern route.

August 2026 attacks continued weekly: Minoan Pioneer (3 Aug, third engineer missing); ADNOC tanker (8 Aug, UAE blamed an Iranian missile); Navig8 Messi and Tarif (13 Aug, UAV strikes); Al Watan (14 Aug); Minoan Dignity (18 Aug, chief engineer killed).

On 17 August 2026 Iran claimed to have DETAINED a UAE-owned tanker in the Strait for not following the Iranian northern route and failing to pay transit service fees - adding a detention risk alongside kinetic attack.

The US naval blockade of all Iranian ports (declared 13 July, effective 2000Z 14 July 2026, JMIC Advisory 015-26) remains fully in force. CENTCOM as of 17 August: 64 commercial vessels redirected, 3 disabled, 2 boarded for compliance verification.

Trump stated on 18 August 2026: 'There are no talks or conversations going on, or scheduled, with the Islamic Republic of Iran. The Naval Blockade remains in full force and effect. The Hormuz Strait is open and operating. All water mines have been removed or detonated.' He posted a map of the strait captioned 'New US Territory' and has threatened to bomb Oman if it interferes.

Iran's Supreme National Security Council set six conditions (8 Aug 2026) for reopening: end US threats/insults; permanently end attacks on Iran and its allies in Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen and Iraq; lift the naval blockade and withdraw US forces; pay war reparations for two 'imposed wars'; lift sanctions; unconditionally release frozen assets.

Iran and Oman have agreed route coordinates for a 'shipping map' and are in 'final stages' of a bilateral transit arrangement, but Iranian officials (FM Araghchi, negotiator Ghalibaf) insist this does NOT constitute reopening the strait.

A senior Iranian official told Reuters on 17 August 2026 that Tehran will escalate and conduct a 'timely and precise' military attack to break the US naval blockade if the US does not fully implement the June deal within weeks.

Traffic collapse: pre-war baseline ~138 vessels/day (JMIC 2025 baseline). Week to 7 Aug: 18 outbound + 21 inbound full transits, about 4% of pre-conflict averages; AIS-detected traffic ~90% below pre-conflict levels. Week to ~16 Aug: 95 transits, down 19.5% week-on-week, with only 3 vessels crossing on 16 August.

Route coercion is working: the Iranian unilateral route carried ~90% of Hormuz traffic in 15-22 July (vs 60/40 Iranian/Omani during the truce), and ~70% of traffic was untraceable via AIS in late July.

War risk hull premiums stand at 7.5-10% of hull value (Marsh/S&P Global Platts), versus ~0.25% pre-conflict and ~1-3% during the late-June post-MoU lull. That is $7.5-10 million per transit for a $100m tanker versus ~$250,000 pre-war; a 270,000-DWT VLCC can pay near $21m. Premiums have NOT decayed despite partial traffic recovery.

EIA data: oil and petroleum liquids through Hormuz averaged 4.9 million b/d in Q2 2026, down from 21.6 million b/d in Q4 2025. EIA assumes flows remain severely constrained through August, rising gradually from September.
Kpler has pushed its base case for a durable Hormuz reopening back to early 2027, shifting from a de-escalation scenario to a prolonged-conflict scenario.
